items.title: 为何英伟达而非Alphabet是持有SpaceX 1.75万亿美元IPO预期下最佳AI股票
items.snippet: 分析在SpaceX即将上市背景下，Nvidia相比Alphabet更适合作为AI投资标的，具备更强增长潜力。
items.raw_snippet: # Why Nvidia, Not Alphabet, Is the Best Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stock to Own for the Expected $1.75 Trillion SpaceX IPO. Nvidia and Alphabet both stand to profit from SpaceX's upcoming IPO. **Alphabet**'s (GOOGL 0.15%) (GOOG 0.28%) early investment in SpaceX is poised to deliver a generous paper gain, while **Nvidia** (NVDA 1.45%) is quietly positioned to secure sustained growth from the very hardware and artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure that the company must scale following its public listing. Let's explore how both AI giants are connected with SpaceX and assess which one is better positioned for the space race in the long run. According to filings, the SpaceX IPO could approach a valuation of $1.75 trillion or higher, with the potential to raise $75 billion in fresh capital. Investors who invest in Nvidia stock before the SpaceX IPO essentially buy clear, leveraged exposure to the hardware ripple effects that could turn SpaceX's public listing into one of Nvidia's next growth catalysts beyond data centers.

items.raw_snippet: # Ineffable Intelligence: $1.1 Billion Seed Funding At $5.1 Billion Valuation Raised For Reinforcement Learning AI. Follow Pulse 2.0 on LinkedIn. A new artificial intelligence startup founded by a former Google DeepMind leader has raised a record-breaking seed round, according to a CNBC report, underscoring surging investor appetite for next-generation AI systems. Ineffable Intelligence, founded by renowned AI researcher David Silver, secured approximately $1.1 billion in seed funding, one of the largest early-stage financings ever recorded. The round values the company at roughly $5.1 billion and includes participation from major global investors, including Nvidia and Google, as well as leading venture capital firms. The company, launched in late 2025 and headquartered in London, is focused on developing advanced AI systems based on reinforcement learning rather than traditional large language models. The involvement of major technology players, including Nvidia and Google, reflects strategic interest in shaping the next wave of AI infrastructure and capabilities.

items.title: 中国政府禁止Meta收购Manus
items.snippet: 中国监管机构以反垄断为由阻止Meta对AI Agent产品Manus的收购交易，维护市场公平竞争。
items.raw_snippet: # Chinese Government Prohibits Meta's Manus Acquisition. The Chinese government has ordered the prohibition of Meta’s acquisition of the Chinese artificial intelligence (AI) startup “Manus.” The decision came approximately four months after authorities launched an investigation in January into whether the $2 billion (approximately 3 trillion Korean won) deal violated China’s technology export regulations. This marks the first time the Chinese government has directly intervened in capital-raising, acquisition, or merger activities by overseas-based “Chinese” companies. The tech industry assessed that “China has begun cutting off investments from U.S. capital to prevent the outflow of domestic AI talent and technology.”. According to China’s foreign investment law, if a specific foreign capital investment is deemed a threat to national security, the Chinese company receiving the investment is obligated to restore the company to its pre-investment state. In the Chinese tech industry, there are expectations that the so-called “Manus effect”—cutting off U.S. capital and preventing the departure of core technical personnel and executives—will spread.

items.snippet: ## SpaceX has struck a deal giving it the right to buy AI coding startup Cursor ...
items.raw_snippet: ## SpaceX has struck a deal giving it the right to buy AI coding startup Cursor for $60 billion – or pay $10 billion for the partnership if no acquisition happens – as it looks to shore up its AI story ahead of a potential IPO. ## SpaceX has the right to buy Cursor, the AI coding startup now at $1B ARR, for $60 billion, or pay $10 billion if the deal never closes, just weeks after filing to go public. SpaceX has struck one of the most unusual deals in AI so far this year, agreeing to pay Cursor, the fast-growing AI coding startup, either $60 billion to acquire it outright or $10 billion for the work the two companies do together if no acquisition happens. It also gives SpaceX something it has been visibly short on: a credible foothold in the one corner of AI that is minting revenue fastest.

items.raw_snippet: # Private firms double down on AI to drive returns and efficiency gains, report finds. Private companies are accelerating investment in artificial intelligence and digital transformation, signaling a growing focus on measurable returns and operational performance, according to a new survey. The Deloitte survey shows that 71% of private company leaders are prioritizing revenue growth over the next 12 months, while 62% are focused on boosting productivity; two areas where AI deployment is increasingly expected to deliver tangible results. Nearly two-thirds (63%) of respondents said their firms are actively investing in digital transformation initiatives, including AI, compared with just 33% that remain in limited or pilot phases. The data points to a widening gap between larger and smaller firms—an important consideration for investors evaluating private market opportunities. “Many are starting to see returns, and continuing the momentum will depend on how they integrate AI across leadership, governance, and the workforce.

items.title: AI disruption puts focus on long-term value of US equities, Goldman ...
items.snippet: * Goldman Sachs said AI disruption is increasing risks tied to long-term U.S. st...
items.raw_snippet: * Goldman Sachs said AI disruption is increasing risks tied to long-term U.S. stock market valuations. * Terminal value now represents roughly 75% of S&P 500 equity value, near a 25-year high. AI’s potential to disrupt businesses has sparked concerns over the dependency of U.S. equity valuations on long-term growth forecasts, particularly in the software sector, Goldman Sachs said. “Terminal value” – a company’s worth beyond the next 10 years based on estimated earnings – accounts for about 75% of the S&P 500’s equity value, near a 25-year high, the Wall Street brokerage said. “Today’s share of value in the terminal value is elevated versus history and mirrors other periods where investor long-term growth expectations were increasingly optimistic, including the dotcom boom,” Goldman Sachs said in a note on Thursday.

items.title: Meet The $250 Million Startup Challenging Salesforce With AI Agents
items.snippet: # Meet The $250 Million Startup Challenging Salesforce With AI Agents. Actively ...
items.raw_snippet: # Meet The $250 Million Startup Challenging Salesforce With AI Agents. Actively AI has raised $45 million to scale up its AI sales agents, which can automate a chunk of the work reps typically do manually. Now, New York-based startup Actively AI is betting its AI agents can do much of that work autonomously — and it’s coming for Salesforce’s crown. Instead of relying on human reps to manually track and prioritize hundreds of accounts, Actively creates a custom AI agent for each one. Built on top of existing large language models and trained on a company’s historical data, the agent can do research for its account, draft outreach, build presentations and flag what reps have missed to suggest next steps. “If you had unlimited money, you’d hire a million sales reps and put one on each company,” says Actively cofounder and CEO Mihir Garimella, 26. Salesforce is down about 30% in 2026, but it’s betting it can stay competitive with its own AI product, Agentforce.

items.title: 苹果下一任CEO需推出杀手级AI产品
items.snippet: WIRED指出，Tim Cook继任者必须发布突破性AI产品，以扭转苹果在生成式AI领域的落后局面。
items.raw_snippet: # Apple’s Next CEO Needs to Launch a Killer AI Product. Tim Cook was a great CEO, but he didn’t crack AI. It’s job number 1 for John Ternus. Sometime in the next year or two, Apple’s new CEO, John Ternus, will step onto a stage and tell the world that his company has a revolutionary product. This product, he’ll say, will put the full and awesome power of AI into everyone’s hands. But if it all works out, that keynote will mark the moment when Apple did to AI what it has done for desktop computers, the internet, mobile technology, wearables and music distribution. That is, it’ll offer a solution to a troublesome technology that’s so delightful and *right* that it seems obvious in retrospect. Current CEO Tim Cook, who announced last week that he’ll vacate his role in September and become the company board’s executive chairman, has done a superlative job guiding the company after Steve Jobs, but he left this important box unchecked.

items.raw_snippet: HomeBusinessCustomers Bank CEO uses AI clone on earnings call to signal automation push. # Customers Bank CEO uses AI clone on earnings call to signal automation push. ## Customers Bank CEO Sam Sidhu said an AI clone delivered part of the lender's earnings call. The moment underlined the bank's wider push to use OpenAI tools across lending, onboarding and operations. In a move that surprised analysts, the CEO of Customers Bank revealed that the voice delivering part of his company’s earnings call was not his own, but an artificial intelligence clone. Sidhu said the use of an AI clone was intended to signal how seriously the bank is approaching AI adoption. The bank is aiming to use AI not just for productivity gains but as a core part of its operating model. The use of an AI clone on an earnings call may have drawn attention, but the broader story is about how artificial intelligence is beginning to reshape banking operations.

items.raw_snippet: -- Elon Musk, the Tesla CEO, world's richest man and OpenAI cofounder, took the stand Tuesday in a high-stakes trial revolving around a bitter feud with his former friend Sam Altman that could reshape the future development of artificial intelligence. Musk filed the lawsuit against Altman and his top lieutenant, Greg Brockman, along with Microsoft over its investments in OpenAI, in 2024. In the civil lawsuit, Musk accuses Altman and Brockman of double-crossing him by straying from the San Francisco company's founding mission to be a steward of a revolutionary technology. In his opening statement, Musk's attorney, Steven Molo, quoted OpenAI's mission statement when it was created as a nonprofit for the benefit of humanity, not constrained by the need to generate financial enrichment for anyone. By 2017, about two years after OpenAI's founding, it became clear that OpenAI would need more money, and Molo said the founders eventually settled on the idea of creating a for-profit arm of OpenAI that would support the nonprofit.

items.raw_snippet: What’s not mysterious is that Apple has struggled with AI and it will now be up to him to make Apple a real AI player. When Apple rolled out hardware chief John Ternus as the CEO to replace Tim Cook, the reaction was kind but muted. That’s because Ternus has said nothing yet to indicate he has a specific plan to position Apple for the future. I have long been a fan of Apple, but the “i” people have a lot of problems. But the truth is that Apple has spent years without the passion and drive that marked the second coming of Steve Jobs as CEO. The promise of AI was intriguing, but Apple didn’t deliver. As for AI, I would love for the iPhone to actually be intelligent about all of the data swimming within its case. One of the critical talents a CEO at a company as large as Apple needs is either vision or a passion that can pass for vision.

items.snippet: ### The Relevance Protocol — Staying Valuable in the Age of AI. Artificial intel...
items.raw_snippet: ### The Relevance Protocol — Staying Valuable in the Age of AI. Artificial intelligence is restructuring the economics of human labor. It’s visible in earnings calls, hiring freezes justified by “efficiency gains,” and the disappearance of roles that existed eighteen months ago. The question is no longer whether AI will affect your work, but how much and how soon. It’s not affecting all jobs at once and doesn’t follow a clean sequence from white-collar to blue-collar work. When a job consists mostly of tasks AI can perform cheaper and faster, its market value compresses:. A plumber’s work remains valuable because of physical presence, liability, and the cost of robotic dexterity. In fact, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says the availability of plumbers and electricians is one of the hardest bottlenecks in the construction of AI data centers. The goal is to extend your economic relevance during a period when the value of undifferentiated cognitive labor is falling. None of this is career advice in the conventional sense.

items.raw_snippet: Altman live updates: Musk testifies in trial that could change the path of AI. Altman: Jury selected in trial that could alter AI's future. (KGO) -- Technology tycoons Elon Musk and Sam Altman are poised to face off in a high-stakes trial revolving around the alleged betrayal, deceit and unbridled ambition that blurred the bickering billionaires' once-shared vision for the development of artificial intelligence. The trial, which is scheduled to begin Monday with jury selection, centers on the 2015 birth of ChatGPT maker OpenAI as a nonprofit startup primarily funded by Musk before evolving into a capitalistic venture now valued at $852 billion. The civil lawsuit accuses Altman, OpenAI's CEO, of double-crossing Musk by straying from the company's founding mission to be an altruistic steward of the technology. Musk recounted his version of OpenAI's founding, which he said essentially happened because of a discussion he had with Google co-founder Larry Page, who called him a "specieist" for elevating the survival of humanity over that of AI.
